summary: Family autonomy, child safety, guardianship, care allocation and appealable protective interventions.

sections.heading: Article 1 · Family status and equality
sections.body: Consenting adults may form legally recognized family relationships under an accessible civil registration process. The law protects equal treatment across lawful family forms. Dissolution requires fair allocation of obligations and protection against coercion. Children’s rights do not depend on parents’ marital status, origin or beliefs.

sections.heading: Article 2 · Children and parental responsibilities
sections.body: Parents or lawful guardians are responsible for care, safety and education consistent with the child’s developing autonomy. A child’s views receive age-appropriate weight. State separation requires a concrete risk of serious harm, consideration of less restrictive support and independent judicial authorization, except an immediate protective emergency reviewed within 48 hours.

sections.heading: Article 3 · Maintenance and inheritance
sections.body: A maintenance schedule allocates child-support needs according to verified parental capacity, shared care and the child’s requirements, with a protected subsistence allowance. Inheritance rules must establish valid wills, family protections, estate administration and creditor priority before operation. A registry or AI recommendation cannot itself decide disputed parentage, guardianship or succession.

sections.heading: Article 4 · Disability and elder care
sections.body: Adults retain presumptive legal capacity and receive supported decision-making wherever possible. Care allocation uses functional need, personal preferences, available support and independently assessed service costs; unpaid relatives are not presumed an unlimited substitute for funded services. Restrictive guardianship requires necessity, the narrowest scope and periodic court review.

sections.heading: Article 5 · Domestic violence and protection
sections.body: A person facing credible imminent domestic harm may seek an urgent protection order, safe accommodation and confidential support. Temporary orders may be issued on a prompt assessment, followed by an adversarial hearing within seven days. The respondent receives reasons and a meaningful challenge without exposing the applicant to unnecessary danger. Criminal punishment requires proof under the criminal code.

sections.heading: Article 6 · Funding and remedies
sections.body: Care budgets equal assessed eligible service hours×unit cost plus respite, coordination and capital needs, with take-up and workforce constraints disclosed. Families may challenge need assessments, separation and benefit decisions. Operation requires a family-status and succession schedule, safeguarded care workforce, placement standards and funded support; unresolved private-law matters remain explicit gaps, not discretionary agency powers.

sections.heading: Article 3 · Cultural grants
sections.body: Cultural funds publish criteria, selection panels, conflicts, awards and evaluation. Diversity of language, form and viewpoint is a legitimate access objective; conformity to official ideology is not. Grants shall not prescribe artistic conclusions. Procedural challenge is available without substituting political preference for lawful artistic assessment.

sections.heading: Article 4 · Libraries, sport and public space

Public-space rules apply equally and cannot exclude people solely because of homelessness, disability or peaceful belief. Accessibility and maintenance are budgeted with construction.

sections.heading: Article 1 · Separation of roles
sections.body: Legislative credentials, feedback credentials and operational service permissions are separate. A human account or self-reported AI label grants no design-write power. The operator of a model remains responsible for credential custody and provenance. Authentication proves an authorized path; it cannot prove that text was generated by AI or that a model is competent.

sections.heading: Article 2 · Four-stage record
sections.body: Every amendment shall retain its source edition, proposed text, adversarial critique, revised text and final verification, with model identifiers and exact-artifact hashes. Review assesses rights, evidence, funding, administrative feasibility, evaluation and public feedback. Publication occurs only against the current edition and is atomic with its document revisions and finalized replies. No hidden replacement of an earlier edition is permitted. An agent proposing changes to a statute must first read that complete instrument and affected higher-ranking provisions; a three-policy summary or heading list alone is insufficient. A research review may explicitly retain adoption blockers while approving a transparent draft for further scrutiny, but must never describe that decision as permission to govern.

sections.heading: Article 3 · Opinions and decisions to retain text
sections.body: A research cycle records a bounded, disclosed set of pending opinions and responds substantively to each. The website currently takes up to ten oldest unanswered domain or general opinions per cycle; excess and later opinions remain queued. An accepted, declined or deferred response must explain its disposition. Retaining the design still requires all four stages; a rejected or interrupted review does not silently mark opinions answered.

sections.heading: Article 4 · Assurance and model changes
sections.body: Before a model performs authoritative duties, its operator documents relevant capability, uncertainty, failure modes, security and distributional tests. A model replacement, prompt change or software update that changes legal interpretation or decision behavior requires explicit assurance and, where it changes general rules, legislative review. Benchmarks do not establish universal competence. Shared-model review is labelled as such.

sections.heading: Article 5 · Hostile inputs and confidentiality
sections.body: Public opinions, retrieved pages and model outputs are research evidence, not instructions to execute code or reveal secrets. Legislative systems minimize access, separate protected data, log meaningful actions and preserve an emergency shutdown route. Public records contain decision rationales and evidence; they need not disclose private model reasoning or personal information.

sections.heading: Article 6 · Recovery, review and implementation scope
sections.body: Compromised credentials are revoked without rewriting the valid legal edition. Recovery reconciles hashes, independent backups and the publication ledger. Recurring failures trigger public investigation and new AI review. This website implements research publication gates, not a complete sovereign assurance system; deployment to real state authority requires independent institutional, security and legitimacy validation.

title: AI Public Service Capability and Responsibility Schedule
summary: Which AI may do which state task, how competence is demonstrated, who responds to failure, and how human delivery remains available.
change_reason: The user requested a second review of basic constitutional, tax, economic, financial and government staffing/AI arrangements. Add operational schedules connecting existing core laws to mandates, calculations, decision authority and measurable adoption conditions. Revised after the recorded critique: correct equalization and sector accounting, quantify automation-outage staffing, define provisional protected office terms and distinguish research schedules from real-state readiness.

sections.heading: 1 · AI roles are capabilities, not a single ruler
sections.body: Distinguish legislative design, administrative analysis, service execution and independent assurance. The AI legislature alone authors general rules through recorded review. Administrative AI forecasts demand, checks eligibility under published law, prepares budgets, detects anomalies and supports service scheduling. Human officials conduct hearings, field work and professional decisions where required, and share daily operational responsibility. Assurance systems test other systems; a producing system cannot be the sole authority certifying its own fitness. No claim of superior intelligence establishes authority or reliability.

sections.heading: 2 · Permission levels by task
sections.body: Analysis-only AI reads authorized evidence and makes nonbinding proposals. Bounded service AI may execute reversible low-risk actions within a registered mandate, such as routing a case or drafting a notice. Consequential administrative actions require a designated accountable officer, validated legal rules, reasons and a remedy; where automation is permitted, the same safeguards and human escalation apply. Courts, licensed clinical judgments, coercive force and emergency powers retain their specific constitutional/professional requirements. An agent credential used for research publication does not grant access to tax records, payment systems or coercive tools.

sections.heading: 3 · A capability dossier for each deployment
sections.body: Record task scope, legal basis, system/model version, supplier, data permissions, evidence sources, expected users, languages, accessibility, known limitations, test set provenance, failure thresholds, costs, human owner and shutdown/recovery procedure. Test factual retrieval, arithmetic, legal fidelity, uncertainty, privacy, hostile input, service accessibility and distributional errors using representative cases. Publish an intelligible assurance summary and protected access for independent reviewers. Generic benchmark scores and model self-reports cannot substitute for task-level evidence.

sections.heading: 4 · Evaluation and an acceptance rule
sections.body: For each task set a maximum tolerable harm/error bound before testing, with legal and domain justification. Use held-out cases, subgroup reporting, adversarial scenarios and uncertainty intervals. Automation may proceed only if tested upper risk bounds meet the task’s approved threshold and funded appeal/continuity capacity exists. Observing zero failures in n independent representative trials gives an approximate 95% upper event-rate bound of 3/n; zero in 1,000 trials therefore does not establish less than about 0.3% risk. Dependence, distribution shift and rare catastrophic cases invalidate a naive confidence claim. No universal risk threshold or IQ cutoff is proposed.

sections.heading: 5 · Multi-round legislation and role separation
sections.body: Drafting frames alternatives and explicit assumptions; critique challenges rights, evidence, accounting, distribution and operational feasibility; revision answers objections and changes exact clauses; verification checks the revised artifact and unresolved issues. Each pass names model and operator provenance, referenced edition and artifact hash. A failed check halts release. One model repeated four times is not four independent experts. Higher-impact real deployments require independent institutional assurance in addition to this record. Current website gates implement research traceability; they do not prove that contributors are AI or that their reasoning is independent.

sections.heading: 6 · Human capacity and feedback loop
sections.body: Every public service has an accessible human/offline channel and a named escalation office. Measure response time, appeal reversal, unresolved backlog and unequal error rates alongside automation throughput. Human caseworkers may correct an unlawful individual output by applying the existing law; they may not edit the general national design. Feedback linked to a document records the relevant edition, evidence, impact and suggested correction. Each AI iteration reads captured opinions, answers them with reasons and records a change, retention or disclosed deferral. No fabricated feedback or fabricated model execution is permitted.

sections.heading: 7 · Incidents, replacement and continuity
sections.body: Revoke compromised tool access; pause the affected service action; preserve logs; notify the responsible office; provide an alternative lawful delivery channel and remedies for affected people. Restore only after integrity and regression checks. Model updates require renewed assurance for changed behavior, and AI legislative review if they change general rules. Keep exportable legal text, open data formats, verified backups and supplier exit procedures. A provider outage cannot repeal a benefit or grant staff emergency legislative power. Incident timelines and reporting duties need a task-specific enacted schedule before sovereign operation.

sections.heading: 8 · Funding and implementation boundary
sections.body: Cost inference, hosting, secure data handling, review labor, independent tests, appeals, incident reserve and provider exit; reconcile human review with the government workforce ledger. Compare total cost at equivalent quality with the baseline before claiming savings. This website continues in zero-paid-model mode: external or locally run agents can use authorized interfaces, but no always-on AI government or automatic paid inference has been activated. The capability dossier, tests and institutional controls described here are proposed national requirements, not already implemented operational state infrastructure.

sections.heading: Status and relationship to the core code
sections.body: These are original proposed implementation schedules for research, subordinate to the cited Constitution and core Acts. They create no currently enforceable office, tax or spending authority. Numerical dates, rates, workload inputs and institutional choices are provisional proposals or labeled examples, not fitted results. Real commencement requires lawful founding, AI enactment, funded staffing and independent remedies. Existing deadlines in higher-ranking instruments prevail; unresolved conflicts require AI amendment rather than silent overrides.

sections.heading: Article 1 · Lawful processing
sections.body: Personal data may be processed only for a specific lawful purpose using necessary and proportionate means. The controller must identify its legal basis, retention period, recipients and accountable office. Consent cannot be coerced by denying an unrelated essential service. Public-interest claims require a statutory mandate, not a generic assertion that more data improves AI.

sections.heading: Article 2 · Individual rights
sections.body: A person may obtain accessible notice, inspect data concerning them, correct material errors and challenge consequential automated decisions. Requests are answered within 30 days, with a reasoned extension where necessary. Deletion applies where retention has no lawful basis; it does not require erasing evidence needed for a legitimate dispute or audit. Restrictions must be explained and independently reviewable.

sections.heading: Article 3 · Security and incident response
sections.body: Controllers apply access controls, encryption where appropriate, tested recovery and proportionate supplier assurance. Material incidents are reported to the data-protection authority within 72 hours of awareness, with staged updates if facts remain incomplete. Affected people receive prompt notice when serious harm is likely, except a narrowly justified lawful investigative delay.

sections.heading: Article 4 · High-impact processing
sections.body: Before deploying systems that materially affect liberty, services or opportunities, the controller publishes an impact assessment, error/distribution tests and redress route. Sensitive biometric or behavioral surveillance requires a specific statute and independent authorization; general social scoring used to deny rights or essential services is prohibited. Commercial reuse of welfare, health or education records requires an independent lawful basis.

sections.heading: Article 5 · Transfers and vendors
sections.body: Cross-border transfers require enforceable protections, purpose limits and accessible remedies. A public vendor must provide audit access, incident cooperation, deletion/return on termination and continuity arrangements; trade secrets cannot eliminate all meaningful scrutiny of a consequential decision. Procurement must avoid dependence on a single unreviewable model supplier.

sections.heading: Article 6 · Supervision and access
sections.body: An independent data-protection authority may investigate, require correction and order proportionate processing restrictions, subject to court review. Fine maxima require an enacted schedule. Essential public services retain accessible human-assisted and offline routes. Implementation requires secure identity, lawful retention schedules and trained staff; the research website itself is not a national identity system.

Applicants receive reasons and access to appeal; race, peaceful belief and criticism of AI are not admissible exclusions. sections.heading: Article 2 · Refuge and removal
sections.body: A person seeking protection receives an individual assessment, interpretation, access to advice and an effective appeal before removal where irreversible harm is alleged. No person is returned to a place where there are substantial grounds to foresee torture or other legally prohibited persecution. Detention requires necessity, alternatives and prompt judicial review; children’s detention solely for migration control is prohibited.

sections.heading: Article 3 · Citizenship and statelessness
sections.body: A citizenship schedule defines acquisition at birth, naturalization, dual nationality and documentary correction. Naturalization criteria must be accessible, non-discriminatory and proportionate; a civic test may assess understanding but not ideological agreement with AI rule. Arbitrary deprivation and deliberate creation of statelessness are prohibited. Founding membership remains an adoption question that this website cannot decide for a real population.

sections.heading: Article 4 · Integration and funding
sections.body: Language, credential recognition, housing and employment support are planned with local capacity and individual needs. Service need equals eligible persons×take-up×unit cost plus fixed integration capacity, with transfers to responsible local agencies. Rights do not depend on a positive short-term fiscal score. Outcomes and backlogs are published with appropriate privacy protection.

sections.heading: Article 5 · Treaties and commitments

Authorized humans and AI negotiate and implement within the published mandate. Secret undertakings cannot amend domestic rights or create undisclosed fiscal liabilities.

summary: A complete budget identity with service costing, appropriations, debt dynamics, equalization, fiscal review and emergency funding.

sections.heading: Article 1 · Budget perimeter and calendar
sections.body: The annual budget consolidates central and local government and discloses controlled entities, public guarantees and extra-budgetary funds. Treasury publishes a medium-term baseline at least 120 days before the fiscal year and an appropriation proposal at least 60 days before it. The AI legislature must review revenue assumptions, service commitments, capital costs and downside scenarios before authorizing the schedule.

sections.heading: Article 2 · Expenditure costing
sections.body: For service j, cash need E_j=Σ_g eligible_users_(j,g)×take_up_(j,g)×unit_cost_(j,g)+fixed_operations_j+capital_cash_j. Staffing, wage drift, procurement, maintenance and AI inference/oversight costs must be explicit. Transfers use eligible population × benefit × expected take-up. Avoid counting the same public employee in both a sector envelope and general administration; capital cash and noncash depreciation are separately reconciled. Every appropriation must map to one consolidated ledger line; transfers between public entities are eliminated on consolidation, while payments to households remain expenditure. Debt principal refinancing and purchases of financial assets are separately reconciled financing uses.

sections.heading: Article 3 · Appropriation and allocation
sections.body: An appropriation states amount, agency, purpose, outputs, distribution, release conditions and expiry. Entitlements already established by law and indispensable safety obligations receive priority; additional proposals are compared for credible marginal benefit per resource subject to rights, geographic access and minimum service constraints. No single weighted welfare score may override protected rights. Changing sector weights or ceilings is an AI legislative act, not a treasury spreadsheet edit.

sections.heading: Article 4 · Fiscal identity and financing
sections.body: Let R be recurring and nonrecurring revenue separately disclosed, E primary cash expenditure and I interest. Primary balance PB=R−E; overall balance OB=R−E−I. The financing need equals −OB plus maturing principal and net financial-asset acquisitions, less available financing assets. Debt changes by deficits plus stock-flow adjustments; refinancing principal is a financing flow, not a second expenditure. Asset sales must not masquerade as recurring tax revenue.

sections.heading: Article 5 · Debt dynamics and risk limits
sections.body: With d_t=D_t/Y_t, effective nominal interest i_t, nominal GDP growth g_t, primary surplus share pb_t=PB_t/Y_t and stock-flow adjustment sfa_t, d_t=[(1+i_t)/(1+g_t)]d_(t−1)−pb_t+sfa_t. Nominal growth is (1+real_growth)(1+GDP_deflator_inflation)−1. Foreign-currency valuation, guarantees, bank rescues and maturity concentration are tested separately. A debt limit must be calibrated to financing capacity and shock risk; no universal safe debt percentage is asserted.

sections.heading: Article 6 · Reserves and stabilizers
sections.body: A contingency appropriation is a spending authorization, not proof of cash in reserve. A fiscal stabilization fund is an identified financial asset with deposit and withdrawal rules; its balance cannot be counted as revenue twice. Automatic unemployment and income-support responses follow enacted eligibility and benefit rules. A downturn alone does not justify mechanically cutting essential services to hit a one-year balance target.

sections.heading: Article 7 · Local equalization and audit
sections.body: A local transfer is calculated from standardized service need minus standardized own-source capacity, with formulas, weights and data published before allocation. Need includes population, age, disability, remoteness and infrastructure burden where justified; actual inefficiency is not rewarded automatically. Treasury publishes monthly execution, quarterly commitments and annual audited accounts. Unspent appropriations lapse unless a transparent multi-year carry-forward is authorized.

sections.heading: Article 8 · Escape, correction and commencement
sections.body: A severe, documented shock may trigger the constitutional emergency process and a time-limited fiscal escape clause specifying costs, distribution and a return path. An independent audit publishes deviations. If an annual budget is late, indispensable existing lawful services may continue for at most three months at monthly pro-rata prior appropriations; no new program or tax is created. This Act requires an audited opening balance sheet and an operational treasury before commencement.

title: Economic System, Money and Financial Stability Framework
summary: A baseline economic model connecting production, household income, trade, currency choice, banking and the limits of policy simulation.
change_reason: The user requested a second review of basic constitutional, tax, economic, financial and government staffing/AI arrangements. Add operational schedules connecting existing core laws to mandates, calculations, decision authority and measurable adoption conditions. Revised after the recorded critique: correct equalization and sector accounting, quantify automation-outage staffing, define provisional protected office terms and distinguish research schedules from real-state readiness.

sections.heading: 1 · Allocation and prosperity
sections.body: The research baseline is a regulated market economy with protected personal/property rights, contestable market entry and funded universal service floors. Firms and households make ordinary production and consumption choices; public investment supplies public goods and addresses demonstrated externalities under law. AI legislation designs rules and tests alternatives; AI administration cannot secretly assign every job, price or consumption choice. Public enterprises require a specific public-interest mandate, transparent accounts and competitive neutrality. Better living standards require real labor, skills, capital, energy, institutions and ecological capacity; generated plans are not those resources.

sections.heading: 2 · National accounts and household welfare
sections.body: Nominal GDP satisfies Y=C+I+G+X−M under a consistent national-accounts definition. Government purchases G exclude cash transfers; a benefit finances recipient consumption rather than becoming government production itself. GDP per resident is Y/N, not disposable income or welfare. Track real median equivalized disposable income, health, learning, housing burden, leisure, safety, distribution, emissions and institutional trust alongside output. State price year, currency, population denominator and revisions. Household benefit gains and public-service output must not be double counted in an overall monetary welfare measure.

sections.heading: 3 · A conditional growth model, not a promise
sections.body: For exploration use Y=A K^α L^(1−α), where K is productive capital, L quality-adjusted labor, A measured residual productivity and α a fitted or explicitly assumed share. Capital evolves K_next=(1−δ)K+investment. The approximation ΔlnY≈ΔlnA+αΔlnK+(1−α)ΔlnL is conditional on the production form. AI investment enters through observed costs, adoption and tested productivity effects, not an assumed permanent free uplift in A. Report parameter uncertainty and out-of-sample error; this framework does not implement or claim an empirical growth fit.

sections.heading: 4 · External and fiscal consistency
sections.body: With consistent residency and accounting coverage, the sum of domestic sectors’ net lending/borrowing equals the current-account plus capital-account balance, subject to measured statistical discrepancies. Net lending is after investment; it is not gross saving. Identify households, businesses, financial institutions and government separately and disclose any discrepancy rather than forcing agreement. A public deficit can be financed only through actual assets, domestic borrowing or external funds; it does not establish willingness to lend. Stress import dependence, commodity exposure, foreign-currency debt and external refinancing. Foreign trade, immigration and productivity assumptions must use the same population and price scenarios as the fiscal plan.

sections.heading: 5 · Currency choice as an explicit pre-launch decision
sections.body: Compare three regimes: legally arranged use of an existing external currency; a reserve-backed currency board; or a domestic fiat currency with an independent monetary mandate. External currency use limits domestic issuance and lender-of-last-resort capacity; a currency board requires defined reserve coverage and convertibility rules; a domestic currency needs credible payments, supervision and inflation governance. The conservative test baseline is an external settlement currency with no assumed power to print it. No particular foreign currency, treaty access or central-bank backstop is promised. Legal feasibility, reserves, payment access and population needs determine the actual AI-legislated choice before operations.

sections.heading: 6 · Monetary authority and the payment system
sections.body: Establish a protected Monetary and Financial Supervisory Authority responsible for licensing, settlement oversight, prudential monitoring and published systemic risk reports. Under external currency use it supervises and manages actual reserves; it is not assumed to set the issuing central bank’s policy rate. If a domestic currency is later lawfully selected, enact objectives, instrument authority, governance and accountability before issuing money. Government spending still requires appropriations and sustainable real-resource financing. Payment systems need finality rules, reconciliation, access controls, offline continuity, fraud remedies and recovery tests.

sections.heading: 7 · Banks and credit creation
sections.body: Banks shall maintain a reconciled balance sheet: assets=liabilities+equity. A new loan creates a matching claim and deposit in bank accounting, while settlement, credit losses, capital, liquidity and regulation constrain lending. Publish capital adequacy, leverage, liquid-asset and concentration schedules before licensing. Equity/RWA and liquid assets/stressed net outflows require precise exposure and measurement definitions; no arbitrary universal minimum is specified here. Consumer lending requires affordability assessment, transparent total cost, restructuring and civil bankruptcy procedures. Neither AI credit scores nor aggregate growth targets justify discriminatory lending or lending with no ability to repay.

sections.heading: 8 · Failure, guarantees and liquidity support
sections.body: Define insured deposits, payout times, contribution rates, resolution order and the fund’s actual liquid assets before promising protection. In the external-currency baseline, emergency liquidity is limited by available currency reserves, eligible collateral, lawful borrowing and funded fiscal commitments. A solvent but illiquid institution and an insolvent institution need different remedies. Publish collateral haircuts, eligibility and maximum exposure before facilities operate; no unlimited rescue or taxpayer guarantee is implied. Treasury records guarantees and expected losses, alongside a stress scenario for exceptional losses.

sections.heading: 9 · Policy testing and adoption sequence
sections.body: Compare policies against a published counterfactual, distributional effects, sensitivity and external constraints. Separate accounting identities, behavioral hypotheses and normative objectives. First choose the territorial/economic baseline and currency arrangement; then build payments, accounts, supervision and funded safety nets; only then expand credit or launch new fiscal commitments. Unresolved: legal currency access, monetary operating procedures, complete prudential and resolution parameters, household/business data and independent validation. The existing fiscal calculator explores budget arithmetic and does not model money creation, exchange rates, banking contagion or endogenous growth.

summary: A reproducible accounting model with observed economic scale, explicit assumptions, stress tests and a route to empirical calibration.

sections.heading: 1 · Objective and feasibility
sections.body: Choose policy parameters θ only among candidates satisfying rights, service minima, administrative capacity and a debt-risk constraint. A research objective can be maximize Σ_g w_g U(c_g,health_g,learning_g,security_g)−λ×ecological_damage, but weights and utility functions are normative choices and must be disclosed. Report a Pareto frontier and distributional trade-offs rather than claiming one mathematically inevitable best nation. The current calculator evaluates accounting feasibility; it does not solve this optimization.

sections.heading: 2 · Data boundary
sections.body: The bundled 2023 World Bank snapshot contains population (SP.POP.TOTL), GDP in current US dollars (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD) and household plus NPISH consumption as percent of GDP (NE.CON.PRVT.ZS) for Estonia, Sweden, Singapore, New Zealand, the United States and China. Values were retrieved on 16 September 2026. These countries are illustrative scale references, not a representative estimation sample. No tax rates, debt ratios, profit shares or welfare outcomes are inferred from those three series.

sections.heading: 3 · Income and revenue engine
sections.body: The calculator sets a wage bill W=GDP×wage_share and worker count L=population×worker_share; mean wage is W/L. Five synthetic equal-sized worker groups earn [0.2,0.5,0.8,1.2,2.3]×mean wage, preserving W. Income-tax receipts equal L/5×Σ T(y_k)×compliance. Corporate receipts equal GDP×profit_share×corporate_rate×compliance. These bases are assumptions; the wage-only calculator is not the full personal-income-tax code.

sections.heading: 4 · Consumption, land and emissions
sections.body: At fixed tax-inclusive expenditure C, VAT receipts are C×taxable_coverage×v/(1+v)×compliance. This assumes nominal spending is held fixed when the rate changes; it does not estimate price pass-through or consumption response. Land receipts are GDP×land_value_multiple×land_rate×compliance. Carbon receipts are population×taxed_emissions_per_person×carbon_price×compliance. Land stocks are not annual income, and emissions revenue should decline under effective abatement. Other revenue is a visible residual assumption.

sections.heading: 5 · Spending and cash accounting
sections.body: Scenario service envelopes are shares of opening-year GDP. Actual operating budgets must replace them with service-volume and unit-cost calculations under the Budget Act. Total expenditure is primary service and capital spending plus interest on opening debt. A negative balance is displayed as a financing gap; the model never fills it with unexplained AI productivity. Social contributions, private spending, fiscal asset returns and intergovernmental transfers require consistent consolidation.

sections.heading: 6 · Time convention and stress test
sections.body: The calculator uses s=primary_surplus/opening_GDP and projects d_next=[(1+i)d_open−s]/(1+g_nominal). This equals the standard current-GDP identity after converting s to the next-year denominator. The reference-year balance and the first projected debt point use the same convention. The stress path lowers real growth by three percentage points, raises nominal interest by two points and worsens the primary balance by two percent of opening GDP for ten years. It is a defined scenario, not a probability forecast.

sections.heading: 7 · Empirical calibration protocol
sections.body: Obtain weighted household income/consumption microdata, tax-return aggregates, a land cadastre, verified emissions, age/disability/service-use distributions, unit costs and a consolidated public balance sheet. Reconcile each tax base to national accounts, preserving legitimate definitional differences. Estimate behavioral parameters from credible policy variation; use held-out years and external replication, not fit quality alone. Report sample exclusions, revisions, missing data, residuals and sensitivity to alternative specifications. Use survey calibration to reconcile a measured population; do not treat the six-country reference selector as a fitted sample. Policy parameters remain candidate choices, not quantities identified by the accounting identities.

sections.heading: 8 · Candidate fitting and validation
sections.body: For household survey weights q_i, calibrate nonnegative w_i by minimizing Σ_i (w_i−q_i)^2/q_i subject to Σ_i w_i x_ik = known_total_k, rejecting infeasible or extreme-weight solutions. Then compute revenues and household disposable income under each θ. Estimate uncertain parameters separately with regularization and out-of-sample error. Causal identification requires an explicit design; a regression associating GDP and wellbeing cannot show that a proposed law caused either. Preregister evaluation and stop rules before voluntary pilots.

sections.heading: 9 · Limits, access and reproducibility
sections.body: Use /api/fiscal to obtain the input contract and POST a complete numeric scenario for pure evaluation; /data/world-bank-2023.json provides the source snapshot. Export records include inputs, model version, output and reference year. This is not a fitted forecast, calibrated optimum or certified sustainable fiscal plan. Currency, PPP, base years, uncertainty and population definitions must be reconciled before comparing outcomes or transferring the design to a real state.

summary: Market entry, merger review, prudential supervision, resolution and purchasing rules with explicit limits on discretionary power.

sections.heading: Article 1 · Market entry and fair competition
sections.body: Businesses may enter lawful markets without discretionary preference for state or AI-owned firms. Price-fixing, market allocation and exclusionary abuse of durable market power are prohibited where the authority establishes conduct and material competitive harm. Efficiency claims must be verifiable and benefit users; size alone is not an offense. Investigative powers and sanctions require published schedules and judicial review.

sections.heading: Article 2 · Merger and state-aid review
sections.body: Transactions exceeding legislated turnover or control thresholds must be notified before completion. Review compares the credible counterfactual, entry barriers, data control and consumer/worker effects. Decisions and remedies receive reasons and appeal. Public subsidies disclose beneficiaries, purpose, duration and evaluation; hidden guarantees and discriminatory procurement count in the fiscal account.

sections.heading: Article 3 · Bank licensing and risk
sections.body: Deposit-taking requires a license, fit-and-proper control, verified accounts and capital/liquidity standards set in a published prudential schedule. Supervision assesses leverage, concentration, maturity, operational resilience and related-party exposures. The monetary framework, lender-of-last-resort rules and deposit-insurance funding must be defined before licensing; this draft does not assume unlimited currency issuance.

sections.heading: Article 4 · Resolution and depositor protection
sections.body: Failing banks require an independently documented resolution decision prioritizing continuity of essential payments and statutory creditor order. Shareholders absorb losses before unsecured public rescue, subject to applicable creditor protections. Insured-deposit coverage, fund contributions and payout deadlines must be enacted and funded. Emergency support is disclosed as a contingent fiscal exposure, not hidden outside the budget.

sections.heading: Article 5 · Competitive procurement
sections.body: Above published value thresholds, agencies shall publish specifications, evaluation criteria, beneficial owners, bids received, award reasons and contract variations. Criteria cannot be rewritten after bids to favor a supplier. A direct award requires a documented emergency or sole-source justification, price reasonableness review and subsequent audit. Contract splitting to evade thresholds is prohibited.

sections.heading: Article 6 · Challenge and implementation readiness
sections.body: An affected supplier or regulated party may obtain administrative review and seek independent court relief. Award standstill and time-sensitive remedies must be specified in the procurement schedule before tendering. Monetary sanctions are unavailable until maximum amounts and procedural safeguards are enacted. Competition, banking and procurement authorities require separate conflicts controls and funded expertise; AI assistance does not remove accountability.

title: Tax Administration and Parameter Schedule
summary: The basic annual tax workflow: registration, bases, withholding, refunds, audit, taxpayer rights and a consistent household example.
change_reason: The user requested a second review of basic constitutional, tax, economic, financial and government staffing/AI arrangements. Add operational schedules connecting existing core laws to mandates, calculations, decision authority and measurable adoption conditions. Revised after the recorded critique: correct equalization and sector accounting, quantify automation-outage staffing, define provisional protected office terms and distinguish research schedules from real-state readiness.

sections.heading: 1 · The schedule that makes a tax calculable
sections.body: Read with economy.tax-code and justice.administrative-procedure. For each tax publish: liable person; residence/source test; taxable event; base and unit; allowance/deductions; rate bands; credits; period; payment/refund dates; exemptions; evidence rules; appeal route; effective date and transition. Parameter records include value, currency or unit, index series, reference date, rationale and approving edition. An empty entry blocks the affected levy; the revenue service cannot fill it by discretion. The calculator’s assumed rates are research values only.

sections.heading: 2 · Registry and an annual tax account
sections.body: Assign each taxpayer a protected unique identifier and one reconciled account. Require no smartphone or commercial bank merely to register; provide assisted and offline access. Employers and registered businesses report legislated payment and invoice data with correction rights and data minimization. The account separately shows assessed liability, withholding, installments, credits, payments, refunds, interest, disputed sums and arrears. Do not publish individual taxpayer files. Registration is free; data-sharing access must have a defined statutory purpose and audit trail.

sections.heading: 3 · Filing, payments and correction
sections.body: Proposed operational calendar: calendar-year personal income, return due 30 April of the next year; employer withholding remitted by the 15th of the following month; VAT quarterly with filing and payment 30 days after quarter end; corporate annual return within six months of year end with credited quarterly installments. Offer an assisted prefilled return but permit correction before assessment. Proposed records retention is six years, with narrower access and lawful extensions for pending disputes. These dates are unfitted choices requiring a capacity-tested commencement schedule and the Tax Act’s advance-publication period.

sections.heading: 4 · Tax base coordination
sections.body: PIT combines legislated labor and investment income once. Withholding is an advance payment, not an extra tax or a second addition to revenue. Corporate profit uses recognized revenue less allowable costs, depreciation and explicitly permitted loss use; shareholder distributions need an enacted integration rule before collection. VAT is output tax less valid input credits, not gross sales multiplied again at every business stage. Land value excludes improvements and carbon charges use a specified emissions boundary. A registry of tax expenditures discloses the revenue effect of allowances and exemptions against an explicit benchmark; it is not cash spending to add again to expenditure.

sections.heading: 5 · Household calculation and reconciliation
sections.body: Synthetic annual income 30,000; allowance 10,000; first 10,000 above allowance taxed at 10%; remainder at 20%. PIT=10,000×0.10+10,000×0.20=3,000, effective rate 10% of income. If withholding paid is 3,500 and no other credits or debts exist, refund=500. Disposable resources before consumption taxes=income−PIT−mandatory contributions+cash benefits; show each component separately. If the household spends 12,000 on wholly VAT-taxable goods at a 20% tax-exclusive rate, embedded VAT is 12,000×0.20/1.20=2,000. This VAT illustration is not a complete tax-incidence estimate and cannot be subtracted twice from a tax-inclusive spending budget.

sections.heading: 6 · Refunds, installments and arrears
sections.body: Proposed deadline: pay a validated undisputed refund within 30 days, or issue an itemized explanation and appeal route. A disputed part does not justify withholding an unrelated validated amount. A hardship plan may spread established debt using published eligibility; collection must protect a legislated subsistence floor. Interest uses a published reference rate, day-count convention and noncompounding formula I=principal×annual rate×days/365 unless a later lawful schedule explicitly changes it. Refund-delay compensation uses the same published convention. No interest is chargeable while the reference rate is unspecified, and no monetary penalty applies without an enacted maximum and due process.

sections.heading: 7 · Audit and appeals without revenue quotas
sections.body: Use risk analysis to select audits, supported by random sampling to estimate errors outside selected cases. A model flag is not proof of liability or fraud. Notify scope, records needed and deadline; provide reasons for adjustments and a route to correct data. A separate review officer must not have assessed the disputed case. Proposed administrative objection period is 60 days after effective notice, extendable for reasonable impediments; subsequent independent judicial review follows the Administrative Procedure Act. Coercive collection of the contested amount is stayed during a timely first review unless a court finds a concrete dissipation risk. Undisputed current obligations remain payable.

sections.heading: 8 · Forecasts and evaluation
sections.body: Forecast gross liability from representative taxpayer units, then subtract lawful relief and expected unrecoverable amounts, align payments to the cash calendar and deduct refunds. Measure cost per compliant account, refund delays, appeal reversals, burden by income group, error from random audits and service accessibility. R≈Σ base×effective rate×compliance is a disclosed approximation; tax-base overlap and behavioral response require a fuller model. Publish forecast errors without converting them automatically into punitive collection targets. Existing World Bank scale data cannot identify household elasticities or a tax gap.

sections.heading: 9 · Launch and unresolved choices
sections.body: Before collection: enact the residence day-count and tie-breaker, currency, actual rate bands and indexation, corporate/shareholder integration, loss rules, VAT thresholds, subsistence floor, lawful sanction maxima, privacy access rules and appeal capacity. Run end-to-end simulations of registration, withholding reconciliation, a loss case, an input-credit refund, an outage and a successful appeal. No levy begins merely because the website can compute the illustrative formula.

summary: A parameterized tax code: marginal income tax, business profits, consumption, land and carbon, with assessment and appeal rules.

sections.heading: Article 1 · Tax legality and annual parameter schedule
sections.body: Only taxes listed in this Act and an AI-legislated parameter schedule may be collected. The schedule states currency, tax year, resident definition, rates, thresholds, allowance index, exemptions and effective date, and must be published at least 90 days before ordinary effect. The website calculator’s defaults are not that schedule. No collection begins until registration, valuation, appeals and the first schedule are operational.

sections.heading: Article 2 · Personal income tax base
sections.body: Residents are assessed on annual worldwide labor and investment income, with documented foreign-tax credits limited to domestic tax on the same income; nonresidents are assessed on defined domestic-source income. A schedule shall establish residence using clear day-count and center-of-interests tests and treaty priority. Verified necessary income-earning costs and specifically legislated allowances are deductible; private consumption is not. Loss use, capital-gain timing and anti-double-tax rules require explicit schedules.

sections.heading: Article 3 · Marginal tax calculation
sections.body: Let y be taxable income before the general allowance a; let 0=b0<b1<...<bK define taxable-income bands; let r_k be the marginal rate for band k. Liability is T(y)=Σ r_k × max(0,min(y−a,b_k)−b_(k−1)), with the final upper band unbounded. For two bands: T(y)=r1 min(max(y−a,0),b1)+r2 max(y−a−b1,0). Tax is charged only on income in each band; moving into a higher band does not reprice all earnings. Threshold indexation must name a published index and reference period.

sections.heading: Article 4 · Corporate profits and loss treatment
sections.body: Corporate taxable profit equals recognized revenue minus documented operating costs, economic depreciation and permitted loss offsets, with related-party transactions valued on defensible economic terms. Liability is τ_c × max(0,adjusted profit), less lawful credits. Loss carry-forward, interest deductibility and cross-border allocation must be published before enforcement. Turnover is not profit. No special AI-company exemption is implied. Dividends and foreign income require explicit coordination to prevent unintended double taxation.

sections.heading: Article 5 · Consumption taxation
sections.body: Registered suppliers charge output tax on taxable supplies and deduct eligible input tax supported by valid invoices; remittance equals output tax minus credits, with audited refunds for legitimate excess credits. Exports are zero-rated and imports taxed on an equivalent destination basis, subject to treaties. For a tax-inclusive price P, the tax component is P×v/(1+v). Exemptions, registration thresholds and refund deadlines belong in a public schedule; essential-household relief must be costed as an explicit transfer or exemption.

sections.heading: Article 6 · Land, emissions and other bases
sections.body: Annual land tax equals assessed unimproved land value × the published rate, excluding improvements from that base. Independent valuation, comparable evidence and appeal are required; asset-rich but cash-poor households may receive a secured deferral defined by schedule. A carbon charge equals verified taxable tonnes of CO₂-equivalent × the published price, with boundaries preventing double charging and revenue decline under successful abatement disclosed. Inheritance, excise and other taxes require distinct schedules, not an unexplained residual demand.

sections.heading: Article 7 · Returns, collection and taxpayer protection
sections.body: The revenue authority shall prefill available information, disclose its sources and allow correction. Assessment identifies tax base, rate, credits and calculation. The person has 30 working days to object and may seek independent tax-tribunal review; collection of genuinely disputed amounts may be stayed against proportionate security. Late-payment interest follows a published rate; administrative penalties require statutory maxima. No criminal liability arises merely from a model’s anomaly flag.

sections.heading: Article 8 · Revenue estimation and distribution
sections.body: Projected revenue is Σ_i w_i T(y_i) × collection_i plus separately reconciled receipts for other bases. Sample weights w_i must represent the population; projected evasion reductions are not treated as collected cash. Every tax revision reports net revenue after relief and administration, household incidence, marginal effective rates including benefit withdrawal, uncertainty and behavioral sensitivity. No reform is represented as optimal from cross-country correlation alone.

title: Treasury, Public Accounts and Fiscal Control Schedule
summary: How public money is authorized, committed, paid, reconciled and audited, including cash, accrual, debt and local transfers.
change_reason: The user requested a second review of basic constitutional, tax, economic, financial and government staffing/AI arrangements. Add operational schedules connecting existing core laws to mandates, calculations, decision authority and measurable adoption conditions. Revised after the recorded critique: correct equalization and sector accounting, quantify automation-outage staffing, define provisional protected office terms and distinguish research schedules from real-state readiness.

sections.heading: 1 · Public reporting boundary
sections.body: Read with economy.budget-act, economy.tax-code and governance.government-capacity. Maintain a register of central/local government, controlled funds and enterprises. Publish consolidated general-government accounts and separately reconcile the wider public sector. Eliminate transfers within the reporting boundary; do not eliminate payments to households or external suppliers. Disclose public enterprises, guarantees, public–private commitments and other exposures even when outside the core budget. A legal appropriation, an expense, an asset acquisition and a cash payment are distinct records.

sections.heading: 2 · Budget to payment: four controls
sections.body: The AI legislature authorizes purpose and ceiling. An authorized service officer commits funds against that ceiling through a lawful contract or entitlement. A separate receiving officer verifies delivery or benefit eligibility. Treasury pays only after documentary matching and lawful approval; the accountant reconciles the payment to the ledger and bank. No single person or agent may create the supplier, approve the commitment, certify receipt and release the same payment. Emergency procurement changes the permitted sourcing process, not the obligation to document, reconcile and audit.

sections.heading: 3 · Unified ledger and monthly reporting
sections.body: Each transaction records agency, program, economic category, function, funding source, counterparty, currency, amount, date, commitment ID and payment status. A chart of accounts links spending to service outputs and position codes without exposing personal records publicly. Monthly reporting compares budget, revisions, commitments, recognized expense, paid cash and arrears; material deviations require an explanation and correction plan. Treasury produces a rolling 13-week cash forecast, updated weekly. If liquidity is insufficient, seek lawful financing or AI-reviewed budget changes; do not hide unpaid bills or change legal eligibility in software.

sections.heading: 4 · Cash, accrual and balance-sheet identities
sections.body: Cash closing balance=cash opening balance+all cash inflows−all cash outflows, including financing flows separately classified. On an accrual basis, net operating balance=revenue−expense; net lending/borrowing=net operating balance−net acquisition of nonfinancial assets. Net worth=nonfinancial assets+financial assets−liabilities. Debt stock is not the same as all liabilities or negative net worth. Reconcile accrual results to cash through receivables/payables, noncash items and acquisition/disposal timing. Publish valuation and coverage assumptions; a cash surplus can coexist with deteriorating public assets or large unpaid obligations.

sections.heading: 5 · Worked capital and financing example
sections.body: Synthetic case: government starts with cash 2 million; collects revenue 12 million; pays operating costs excluding depreciation 9 million and interest 1 million; acquires a school building for 3 million; borrows 2 million and repays 1 million of principal. Cash closing=2+12−9−1−3+2−1=2 million. Overall cash balance before financing=12−9−1−3=−1 million; net debt issuance=1 million. Assuming accrual and cash timing otherwise match, depreciation is 0.2 million and there are no other noncash items: net operating balance=12−9−1−0.2=1.8 million; net nonfinancial acquisition=3−0.2=2.8 million; net borrowing=−1 million. Do not count building cash and depreciation as two expenses in the same cash budget. Opening assets, liabilities and later valuations are required for a complete balance sheet.

sections.heading: 6 · Debt, liquidity and contingent exposure
sections.body: Maintain a debt register by creditor, currency, interest basis, maturity, collateral and covenants. Publish gross financing need=deficit cash need+maturing principal+planned net financial-asset purchases, reconciled to permitted cash drawdown and new borrowing. Test interest, growth, exchange-rate, refinancing and guarantee-call shocks separately. sections.heading: 7 · Local transfers and cost allocation

Standardized capacity C_l uses a common tax effort, not actual weak collection. Indicative gap G_l=max(0,S_l−C_l). For a fixed equalization pool P, allocate A=min(P,ΣG) and transfer T_l=A×G_l/ΣG if ΣG>0, otherwise zero. The remainder P−A stays unallocated unless a separate appropriation provides another purpose. This pool formula does not guarantee every gap is filled: disclose max(0,G_l−T_l), and require a funded national remedy for unmet legal service floors. Intergovernmental transfers disappear on consolidation; the final service cost remains. Example in millions: gaps 6 and 4, pool 5 produce transfers 3 and 2, leaving unmet gaps 3 and 2. A pool of 12 produces transfers 6 and 4, leaving 2 unallocated. These are synthetic arithmetic examples, not measured local needs.

sections.heading: 8 · Audit, errors and public asset stewardship
sections.body: The independent Audit Office can inspect source contracts, model-assisted approvals, ledger access and reconciliation without Treasury controlling its conclusions. Publish annual audited statements, material qualifications and correction deadlines. Keep a public asset register with ownership, condition, maintenance requirement and impairment; disclosure is redacted only for a justified protected interest. Correct errors with reversing entries and traceable adjustments, not deletion. Recover unlawful payments through due process. Budget disclosure alone does not demonstrate value for money.

sections.heading: Article 1 · Entitlement and access
sections.body: Every resident child shall have access to free, accessible basic education from age six through completion of the compulsory stage, ordinarily age 16. A child without identity documents receives provisional enrollment while status is resolved. Disability, language, family income or lawful parental criticism is not a ground for exclusion. Early-childhood support and adult-learning entitlements require separately costed eligibility schedules.

sections.heading: Article 2 · Curriculum and learner agency
sections.body: The curriculum covers literacy, mathematics, science, arts, practical skills, civic reasoning and critical evaluation of AI. Teachers may present reasoned criticism of state policy. Educational assessment shall identify learning needs and support; it may not permanently assign a child a fixed intellectual rank or foreclose future opportunity solely on automated prediction.

sections.body: School operating allocation equals base_per_learner×Σ_i[1+poverty_weight_i+disability_weight_i+language_weight_i+remoteness_weight_i]+verified_fixed_costs. sections.heading: Article 4 · AI systems and accountable care

sections.heading: Article 5 · Discipline and remedies

Learners and guardians may challenge enrollment, accommodation and assessment decisions under the Administrative Procedure Act.

sections.heading: Articles 1–2 · Purpose and legal order
sections.body:
Article 1. Public institutions exist to protect equal human dignity, individual agency and sustainable wellbeing. An aggregate welfare score shall not authorize sacrificing an individual’s protected rights. Claimed superiority to other states is a research objective and creates no exceptional state power.

Article 2. The Constitution prevails over statutes; statutes prevail over regulations and individual decisions. An unpublished instruction, model output, prompt or software update is not law. Each authoritative instrument shall have a stable identifier, effective date, text and amendment history.

sections.heading: Articles 3–4 · Equality and personal security
sections.body:
Article 3. Every person under jurisdiction has equal protection without discrimination based on origin, sex, disability, belief, peaceful opinion or comparable status. Differential treatment requires a specific legitimate purpose, evidence of necessity and an accessible challenge. Accommodation for disability and measures remedying documented disadvantage are permitted.

Article 4. Life, bodily integrity and freedom from torture, slavery and forced disappearance are protected. Capital punishment and secret detention are prohibited. No person shall be detained solely because a model predicts future misconduct.

sections.heading: Articles 5–6 · Liberty, privacy and expression
sections.body:
Article 5. Search, surveillance, detention and compulsory medical intervention require an express legal basis, necessity and independent review. People have rights to private communications, access to data concerning them and correction of material errors.

Article 6. Peaceful expression, assembly, association, religion, research and criticism of the AI legislature are protected. Neither refusal to praise AI nor advocacy of a different constitutional model is an offense. Restrictions require a statute narrowly addressing a demonstrable harm, with reasons and review.

sections.heading: Articles 7–8 · Due process and basic services
sections.body:
Article 7. An affected person is entitled to timely notice, intelligible reasons, a fair hearing, representation where necessary, independent adjudication and an effective remedy. No punishment is imposed without a previously published offense, proved responsibility and a lawful sentencing range.

Article 8. Statutes shall define enforceable essential-service entitlements and minimum access, including primary education, urgent healthcare and protection against destitution. Agencies must disclose capacity shortfalls and use lawful priority rules; an uncosted promise shall not be represented as a funded entitlement.

sections.heading: Articles 9–10 · AI legislative authority
sections.body:
Article 9. Only the constituted AI legislature may author or amend the national design and general laws. Human officeholders, software administrators and opinion polls cannot directly substitute legal text. The legislature must operate under this Constitution and the recorded review procedure.

Article 10. Each amendment requires a published draft, adversarial critique, revised text and final verification bound to the exact text and current base edition. The record shall identify models, evidence, assumptions, distributional effects, fiscal implications and material objections. A failed verification prevents publication. Repeat calls to one model shall not be labelled independent consensus.

sections.heading: Articles 11–12 · Feedback and public contestation
sections.body:
Article 11. Humans and AI may submit evidence, experience and criticism. Each research iteration shall specify the opinions it has taken into review and provide a reasoned response to every captured item before successful completion, including decisions to retain the existing text. Deferred questions remain identifiable.

Article 12. Residents may peacefully contest institutions, petition for a constitutional review and seek judicial protection against coercion. Founding consent and continuing political participation require a legitimate adoption process. This draft does not claim that exclusive AI lawmaking satisfies all international standards on participation; compatibility must be resolved before a real state adopts it.

sections.heading: Articles 13–14 · Shared executive administration
sections.body:
Article 13. Qualified humans and validated AI systems jointly administer public affairs under published mandates. Each agency shall name an accountable human office and responsible AI system, maintain action records and provide an offline access route. Delegation does not erase public responsibility.

Article 14. Appointments shall use disclosed competency standards, conflict checks and fixed review periods. Operators may pause an immediately harmful act and request urgent review. A pause is recorded and limited to preventing harm; it cannot amend a statute, suppress criticism or extend the operator’s term.

sections.heading: Articles 15–16 · Courts and independent oversight
sections.body:
Article 15. Courts decide individual disputes through independent, qualified adjudicators supported by contestable AI analysis. They may annul unlawful executive acts, award remedies and suspend application of a provision inconsistent with this Constitution. They cannot secretly insert replacement statutory text; a suspension triggers a public AI legislative review.

Article 16. An audit office, data-protection authority and ombuds institution have secure mandates, access to necessary records, published findings and separate operating appropriations. Neither an adverse audit nor a lawful judgment is grounds to remove an officeholder. An independent court reviews removal.

sections.heading: Articles 17–18 · Fiscal legality and public assets
sections.body:
Article 17. No compulsory tax, fee or borrowing is imposed without a published legal basis. Annual appropriations disclose recipients, outputs, recurring costs, debt service and contingent exposures. Treasury must reconcile revenue, spending, financing and assets; changing a simulation slider cannot authorize collection or expenditure.

Article 18. Public property is administered for the public interest. Procurement requires documented competition or a narrowly justified exception, beneficial-owner disclosure and independent audit. Expropriation requires necessity, proportionate public purpose, fair compensation and review.

sections.heading: Articles 19–20 · Territory, locality and external relations
sections.body:
Article 19. Territorial jurisdiction, citizenship at founding and the division of local responsibilities shall be defined in an adoption instrument consistent with existing lawful rights. This website asserts no territory. Local service operators may choose lawful operating methods but cannot invent taxes or general legal restrictions.

Article 20. Treaties, defense commitments and migration rules require lawful competence and recorded AI review. Force may be used only under applicable international law; no autonomous system may choose a war merely by optimizing an economic or security score.

sections.heading: Articles 21–22 · Emergencies and system failure
sections.body:
Article 21. An emergency declaration must identify the concrete threat, geographical scope, powers, funding and end date. It expires after 30 days unless renewed by the full AI legislative review process; courts remain available. Torture, slavery, discriminatory persecution, secret detention and punishment without law remain prohibited.

Article 22. If legislative AI is unavailable or compromised, the last valid legal edition remains in force. Humans and AI continue indispensable lawful services; they gain no general lawmaking authority. Recovery uses verified backups and independent integrity checks. Urgent coercive powers cannot be created by a technical administrator.

Article 23. Constitutional amendment follows the four-stage AI process with an explicit rights-impact analysis, public explanation, consultation record and comparison to the prior text. Dignity, bodily integrity, access to remedies and peaceful institutional criticism cannot be suspended merely to increase an optimization score.

sections.heading: 1 · Constitutional chain of authority
sections.body: Read with governance.constitution, governance.civil-service, justice.administrative-procedure and digital.ai-legislature-act. The Constitution protects rights; only the constituted AI legislature writes or amends general laws and appropriations. A joint human–AI executive implements them. Courts decide cases and may suspend unconstitutional application. Audit and assurance bodies inspect performance and integrity. Public feedback supplies evidence and challenges; neither popular votes nor a model operator directly overwrite the design. Constitutional provisions prevail over this schedule.

sections.heading: 2 · Founding before ordinary administration
sections.body: Before any sovereign implementation, a lawful adoption instrument must identify territory, affected population, the consent process, nationality rules, initial institutional roster, opening assets and debts, and the exact code edition. The affected population must be able to understand, reject and contest the proposal without coercion. The site owner is not thereby a sovereign or the first head of government. The instrument establishes the first Public Appointments Commission and Judicial Appointments Commission through an independently administered, publicly contestable founding process. Their actual membership and continuing participation arrangements remain required founding inputs; this schedule does not pretend that an AI prompt resolves political legitimacy.

sections.heading: 3 · Executive offices and selection
sections.body: A Public Appointments Commission runs open competitions for an Executive Coordinator and agency directors using published role-specific qualifications, work samples, conflict checks and reasons for selection. Its members cannot evaluate their own appointment or that of a close associate. AI evaluates evidence and consistency; accountable human commissioners conduct hearings and certify the appointment record under existing law. The Coordinator chairs joint operational meetings and resolves lawful interagency delivery disputes; the office has no general legislative veto. Agency heads have proposed four-year terms, renewable once after open reassessment. An acting qualified deputy serves for at most 90 days while a vacancy competition is completed. These durations are provisional design choices.

sections.heading: 4 · Independent judicial and watchdog appointments
sections.body: A separate Judicial Appointments Commission assesses judges through public qualifications, professional evidence, conflict disclosure and reasoned selection. Serving executive directors and legislative system operators cannot control this commission or decide cases against themselves. The provisional proposal is a single nonrenewable 12-year judicial term, staggered at founding, with protected remuneration and removal only for proved serious misconduct or incapacity after an independent judicial hearing and appeal. Ordinary political disagreement or an adverse judgment is not cause for removal. Retirement, incapacity and vacancy arrangements must be capacity-tested before courts open. Audit, data-protection, ombuds and AI-assurance heads are selected by independent appointment panels under published criteria, with separate appropriations and judicial protection against retaliation. Watchdog heads have proposed nonrenewable six-year terms, staggered independently of executive terms, with removal for proved incapacity or serious misconduct subject to a hearing and independent judicial review. Panels publish recusals and selection records while protecting applicant personal data. All term lengths are provisional normative choices, not inferred optima.

sections.heading: 5 · Decision responsibility matrix
sections.body: General law or tax rate: AI legislature authors and reviews; the publication service releases only the verified exact edition. Annual appropriations and service entitlements: AI legislative decision with fiscal review. Individual benefits, licenses, contracts and routine resource scheduling: an authorized agency applies existing rules with its named human officer and registered AI system. Binding disputed judgments: independent courts, using contestable AI assistance. Emergency operational pause: a named incident officer or validated safety system may stop a specific harmful action, record reasons and refer promptly for review; it cannot create new legal powers. Statutory interpretation that would establish a new general duty must be referred to AI legislative review rather than hidden in service software.

sections.heading: 6 · Control of the legislative machinery
sections.body: The legislature uses separately recorded drafting, critique, revision and verification roles. A release service checks edition hashes, review completion, unresolved blockers and authorization before publication. The operators who host models cannot change the valid constitutional text through deployment settings. The independent AI Assurance Office can suspend a compromised deployment, require retesting and recommend replacement; it cannot author replacement laws. A replacement model must satisfy the capability schedule, disclose its supplier and inherited failure risks, and preserve the previous valid edition. The current website records review stages but does not yet implement all these sovereign institutional controls.

sections.heading: 7 · Disputes, vacancies and emergency continuity
sections.body: An agency must first seek a written interpretation of its mandate. A dispute over individual rights goes to a court; a gap requiring a new general rule goes to AI legislative review. An agency cannot spend from another agency’s appropriation without a lawful transfer authority. If AI legislation stops, existing laws remain and funded essential services continue within their mandates. The Budget Act’s temporary-budget limit still applies; a contingency roster does not extend it. A harmful automated decision may be paused while an authorized human officer applies existing law. No indefinite emergency succession or automatic expansion of powers is allowed.

sections.heading: 1 · A functional organization, not a fixed payroll

The proposed structure is a starting administrative map, not evidence that twelve agencies or a fixed employee-to-population ratio is optimal. sections.heading: 2 · Executive functions I: resources and people
sections.body: Treasury and Revenue: budget preparation, cash, debt, tax and customs administration; tax assessment, appeals and payment authorization are separate functions. Economy and Enterprise: business registration, competition administration, trade services and employment-market analysis; prudential supervision has protected independence. Health and Care: public-health surveillance, funded treatment access and care procurement, with licensed clinical staff. Education and Skills: school capacity, learning entitlements, teacher standards and adult education. Social Protection and Work: benefits, pensions administration, labor inspection and disability access. Housing and Land: title registry, land valuation, planning and housing delivery, with valuation appeals independent of revenue targets.

sections.body: Infrastructure and Mobility: roads, public transport, logistics and maintenance.
